children: Urban Company shares rose 7 percent on Wednesday after the home services platform's Rs 2,500 crore qualified institutional placement (QIP) received an overwhelming response from investors.
The stock climbed to a high of Rs 172.45 per share on the NSE, up 7 percent.
The company raised Rs 2,500 crore through the QIP, which attracted bids worth around Rs 15,300 crore, nearly six times the issue size, Moneycontrol reported.

The strong demand came from a diverse group of institutional investors, including domestic mutual funds, foreign portfolio investors and insurance companies, indicating broad-based interest in the Gurugram-based company's shares.

Among the domestic investors that participated in the issue were SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, one of the people cited in the report said.
Urban Company QIP: Rs 2,500 crore QIP oversubscribed 6 times; SBI MF, ICICI Prudential, Goldman Sachs, Norges among bidders
The fresh capital is expected to provide the company with greater financial flexibility to pursue its growth plans and explore organic and inorganic opportunities.
A part of the proceeds will also be used to expand InstaHelp as the company looks to strengthen its position in the increasingly competitive segment.

title: Urban Company shares rise 7% as Rs 2,500 crore QIP oversubscribed
